text.p: A depleted England overwhelmed Argentina 46-20 in the first rugby test on Saturday, snatching the game out of the Pumas' reach in 15 minutes of exhilarating play.
Argentina looked dangerous, and England rather slow on their feet, in the first half though it ended with the tourists just ahead 17-13.
But England re-emerged meaner and more polished in the second half.
Barely a minute after the recommencement of play, a tough series of running passes from right to left field finished with Adedavo Adebayo plunging over the touchline for a try.
Ben Clarke managed to wrestle a try from the bottom of a heaving pack of players and then Mike Catt scooted over the right half of the touchline for another.
Catt converted twice and England -- ahead 36-13 -- put Argentina out of the game within a rampaging quarter of an hour.
The match proved a point for Jack Rowell's England, which only just avoided a humiliating loss to the Pumas at Twickenham in December.
The victory was particularly sweet for being won with a team featuring six new caps, much of England's playing blood having been sapped by the British Lions squad touring South Africa.

Rowell confessed to having feared that the Pumas might win at home and welcomed the result both for the blooding of new players such Tony Diprose and Martin Corry and for its successful demonstration of a new, fast English running game.
"Now the squad has settled we would aspire to play that type of rugby, opponents permitting, all the time," Rowell told reporters.
Captain Phil de Glanville admitted England were under par in the first half, especially in defence.
"In the second half our defence was much better. We managed to steal a lot of balls in the tackle and also the organisation around the rucks and mauls was much better," he said.

The Pumas had come out on to the Ferro Carril Oeste stadium looking to run with the ball and in the first half it looked like they might run round an England who still seemed slightly jetlagged after a couple of weeks in the country.
Gonzalo Quesada scored a try after the ball crossed the field in Argentine passes and Argentina were on England's tail 20 minutes into the game.
Puma captain Lisandro Arbizu put his side ahead at 13 to 10 a few minutes before the end of the first half, after a run begun by a Quesada free kick almost at Argentina's touchline.

But the only other points Argentine scored came about 25 minutes into the second half. Tomas Solari received a ball from a scrum near the England line and ran it in easily in for a third Argentine try. Quesada converted.
The second and final test will be played next Saturday.
Teams:

England: Jim Mallinder, John Sleightholme, Phil de Glanville (captain), Nick Greenstock, Adedavo Adebayo, Mike Catt, Kyran Bracken, Tony Diprose, Ben Clarke, Martin Corry (Sheasby), Nigel Redman, Martin Haag, Darren Garforth, Phil Greening (Hardwick), Kevin Yates.

Argentina: Ezequiel Jurado, Tomas Solari, Eduardo Simone, Lisandro Arbizu (captain), Facundo Soler, Gonzalo Quesada, Nicolas Fernandez Miranda, Pablo Bouza, Pablo Camerinckx, Rolando Martin, Pedro Sporleder (Fernandez Lobbe), German Llanes, Mauricio Reggiardo, Federico Mendez (Promanzio), Roberto Grau.
